summary_paragraph: A 58-year-old woman with type 1 diabetes, bilateral lower extremity amputations, chronic kidney disease, and systolic heart failure was admitted for cough, nausea, and vomiting. She had a productive cough with yellow phlegm and multiple episodes of non-bilious vomiting. Initial evaluation revealed sinus tachycardia, elevated creatinine (2.4), and mild hyperkalemia (5.5). A chest X-ray showed no pneumonia, and symptoms were attributed to a viral upper respiratory infection. Nausea and vomiting were managed with IV and oral antiemetics, and IV fluids were given for dehydration. Urine cultures showed mixed flora consistent with contamination, and blood cultures were negative. Her kidney function improved to a creatinine of 1.9, and electrolytes normalized. Lisinopril was held during admission due to renal impairment and restarted at a reduced dose (5 mg daily) at discharge. Gabapentin was renally dosed, and metoprolol was initiated for secondary prevention after NSTEMI. She tolerated a full diet, symptoms resolved, and she was discharged home with follow-up instructions.
problems: Acute upper respiratory infections of unspecified site
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type I [juvenile type], not stated as uncontrolled
